;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Operations Claw-Eagle and Tiger]], [[Iraq–Turkey relations]]
**[[government of Iraq|Iraq]] cancels a ministerial meeting and summons the [[Turkey|Turkish]] [[ambassador]] as [[Iraq]] blames Turkey for a [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] strike that killed two high-ranking [[Iraqi military]] officers. Officials called it a "blatant Turkish drone attack" in the autonomous [[Iraqi Kurdistan|Kurdish]] region in northern Iraq. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/iraq-fumes-turkey-deadly-drone-attack-200812060149126.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**[[Islamist]] [[insurgent]]s linked to [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] seize control of the port city of [[Mocímboa da Praia]] in northern [[Mozambique]], after days of heavy fighting with [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|government forces]]. Soldiers reportedly abandoned their positions and fled the city on boats after becoming outnumbered, as several fellow soldiers were killed by the militants. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53756692 (BBC News)]
*Clashes between armed civilians and [[South Sudan People's Defence Forces|soldiers]] in [[Tonj]], [[Warrap (state)|Warrap]], [[South Sudan]], during a disarmament exercise leave 127 dead since Saturday, an  army spokesman says. A total of 45 of those killed were part of the security forces while the rest were youths from the area. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/12/S-Sudan-clashes-between-civilians-soldiers-leave-127-dead-Army.html (AFP via Al Arabiya)] 

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[economy of the United Kingdom|economy]] officially enters [[recession]] for the first time since 2009, according to [[Chancellor of the Exchequer|Chancellor]] [[Rishi Sunak]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-53748278 (BBC News)]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[Stonehaven derailment]]
**A [[Abellio ScotRail|ScotRail]] train [[derailment|derails]] near [[Stonehaven]], [[Aberdeenshire]], [[Scotland]], following torrential rain and thunderstorms, killing three people, including the driver. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-north-east-orkney-shetland-53751678 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment	
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports the largest rise of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases since the lockdown was lifted in May, with 2,524 new cases being reported in the last 24 hours. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53747852 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The number of COVID-19 cases in [[Germany]] rises by 1,226, which is the biggest daily rise since May, according to the [[Robert Koch Institute]], as the health minister warns of outbreaks in nearly all parts of the country due to vacation returnees and partygoers. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/germany-records-biggest-jump-in-new-coronavirus-cases-since-early-may/45962278 (Swiss Info)] [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/08/11/world/europe/11reuters-health-coronavirus-germany-cases.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
****[[President of Peru|President]] [[Martín Vizcarra]] bans family gatherings and extends a lockdown to five more [[Regional circumscriptions of Peru|regions]], following a 75% surge in COVID-19 cases among children and adolescents. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-peru/peru-president-bans-family-gatherings-extends-lockdowns-as-coronavirus-infections-spike-idUKKCN2582UK (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
****[[Jorge Rodríguez (politician)|Jorge Rodríguez]], incumbent [[Minister of Popular Power for Communication and Information]] announces he tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2020/08/12/world/americas/ap-lt-virus-outbreak-venezuela.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire]]
****[[Governor of New Hampshire|New Hampshire Governor]] [[Chris Sununu]] issues a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] for gatherings with more than 100 people. Masks will be required at the [[Laconia Motorcycle Week]], which is expected to be held on August 22 and 23. The move comes after few attendees of the [[Sturgis Motorcycle Rally]] in [[South Dakota]] appeared to wear masks. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/new-hampshire-mask-mandate-before-motorcycle-rally/ (CBS News)]
***The United States reports more than 1,500 new deaths caused by COVID-19, making today the deadliest day for the country since the end of May. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/08/13/coronavirus-live-updates.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]	
***Australia suffers the deadliest day of the pandemic when [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports 21 deaths in the last 24 hours. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-victoria-update-410-new-cases-of-covid19-21-deaths/6f20de72-bfcf-4d44-b94b-28e8d347083a (9 News)]

;International relations
*[[Belarus–Lithuania relations]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Lithuania]] allows "unrestricted entry" to all [[Belarus]]ians "for humanitarian purposes" amid anti-government protests and political repression in neighbouring Belarus. Existing COVID-19 restrictions will not apply to Belarusians. [https://www.baltictimes.com/lithuania_allows_unrestricted_entry_to_belarusians__for_humanitarian_purposes_/ (''The Baltic Times'')]
*[[Jordan–Syria relations]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
**[[Jordan]] announces it will close its only trade land border crossing with Syria for a week beginning on Thursday morning after a sharp spike in COVID-19 cases coming from its northern neighbour. [https://www.trtworld.com/middle-east/jordan-to-close-border-with-syria-after-virus-cases-surge-38851 (TRT World)]

;Law and crime
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[Ocala, Florida]], City Council overrides Ocala Mayor Kent Guinn’s veto of the Council's earlier emergency ordinance that requires people to wear masks inside businesses. [https://www.wcjb.com/2020/08/12/ocala-city-council-overrides-ocala-mayor-veto-face-masks-now-required/ (WCJB-TV)]
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Indiana]]
***Two [[Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department|Indianapolis police officers]] are expected to face charges for using excessive force during protests over the [[Killing of George Floyd|death]] of [[George Floyd]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/indiana-cops-charged-battery-protesters-arrests-72332616 (ABC News)]
*[[Hong Kong]] pro-democracy activists [[Jimmy Lai]] and [[Agnes Chow]] are released on bail. Lai makes no comment while Chow says that her arrest amounts to "political persecution and political suppression". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/hong-kong-media-tycoon-lai-released-bail-arrest-200811173810887.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Bougainvillean general election]]
**Elections for the [[Bougainville House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] and the [[President of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville|president]] of [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville|Bougainville]] start taking place. The outcome of the election might have a major impact on the region's future as it follows last year's non-binding [[2019 Bougainvillean independence referendum|independence referendum]] which saw 98% of the voters approving independence from [[Papua New Guinea]]. The election is held a week after the first case of [[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea|COVID-19]] was confirmed in the region and is scheduled to run until the first of September. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/423311/bougainville-election-underway-today (RNZ)]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]	
**[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] delays dissolution of [[Parliament of New Zealand|Parliament]] until 17 August, due to resurgence of COVID-19. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-08-12/jacinda-ardern-parliament-dissolve-covid-outbreak-auckland/12550058?nw=0 (ABC News Australia)]

;Science and technology
*[[Palaeontologist]]s at the [[University of Southampton]] report the discovery of a new species of theropod [[dinosaur]] called ''[[Vectaerovenator inopinatus]]'' on the [[Isle of Wight]], [[England]]. The species belongs to the same group as the ''[[Tyrannosaurus]]'' and modern-day birds. It lived roughly 115 million years ago during the [[Cretaceous]] period. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-hampshire-53738762 (BBC News)]
